title: Abberley Coffee Table in Brown | Kaiku
summary: A 110cm coffee table in a warm brown finish that gives up depth rather than length: at 50cm front to back it leaves the walking gap between sofa and table intact, while the 40cm top sits just below the line of most seat cushions.
tagline: Long enough to share, shallow enough to walk past

sections.heading: A long table on a shallow footprint
paragraphs: Measured, the Abberley is 110cm long, 50cm deep and 40cm high. Most coffee tables of this length are 60cm or 70cm deep, and the extra 10cm to 20cm is what turns a comfortable living room into one where everybody sidesteps the corners.

A shallow rectangle also spreads the useful surface along the sofa rather than out into the room. Two people sitting at opposite ends both have a corner within arm's reach, and nothing has to be slid across a metre of table.

sections.heading: Why the 40cm height matters
paragraphs: Seat cushions on a typical sofa land somewhere between 42cm and 48cm from the floor, so a 40cm table sits just under the seat line. Cups go down and come back up without a lift, and there is no rim standing above the cushion to catch a knee.
bullets: 40cm high — a shade below most seat cushions
50cm deep, so a 90cm walkway survives in a 3m room
110cm of length reads as balanced in front of a two or three-seat sofa

sections.heading: What actually sits on it
paragraphs: Half a metre of depth takes a tray at one end and still leaves room for books, a bowl and a couple of glasses at the other. It is a good table for a room where the sofa faces a television, because at 40cm nothing on the top interrupts the sightline from a seated position.

sections.heading: Weight, moving and care
paragraphs: It weighs 25kg, which is a two-person lift up a flight of stairs and an easy shove across carpet on your own. Dust it with a dry cloth, wipe spills as they happen rather than later, and use a mat under anything hot — we hold no heat rating for the finish, so we will not claim one.

faqs.question: How much walking space does a 50cm deep coffee table leave?
faqs.answer: In a room around 3m across with a sofa against one wall, a 50cm depth typically leaves 80cm to 90cm of clear floor on the far side — enough to walk past without turning sideways. Leave 35cm to 40cm between the sofa and the table itself for legs.

faqs.question: Is a 40cm high coffee table comfortable to reach from a sofa?
faqs.answer: Yes for most seating. Sofa cushions usually sit at 42cm to 48cm, so at 40cm the top is fractionally below the seat and you reach down rather than across. If your sofa is a low, deep design with cushions near 35cm, a lower table would suit it better.

faqs.question: Can one person carry the 25kg Abberley coffee table into place?
faqs.answer: One person can slide it across a floor, but 25kg over a 110cm span is awkward to grip alone — carry it with two people, one at each end, especially on stairs or through a turn.

faqs.question: Will a 110cm table look undersized in front of a large sofa?
faqs.answer: In front of a two or three-seat sofa up to about 220cm, 110cm reads as proportioned. Against a longer sofa or a corner arrangement, the length starts to look short, and a pair of tables or a wider piece usually works better.

faqs.question: Does the brown finish on the Abberley show rings and dust?
faqs.answer: Any dark finish shows dust and dried water marks sooner than a pale one, so a weekly dry cloth and coasters do most of the work. We do not publish a stain or heat rating for this finish, so treat it as you would a lacquered surface: nothing hot, nothing wet left standing.
